---

EDUCATION

M.Sc. Applied Physics
Kymijoki University of Technology, Lappeenranta | 2018
Thesis: Wavelet decomposition methods for industrial vibration monitoring

---

EXPERIENCE

Signal Processing Engineer
Baltic Sensor Networks, Espoo | January 2019 -- present

- Design and maintain acoustic signal processing pipelines for underwater environmental monitoring stations across the Baltic Sea. The propagation modelling draws heavily on the wave physics foundation from my KUT degree, particularly for shallow-water multipath correction.
- Configure and commission hydrophone arrays at installation sites in Finland, Estonia, and Latvia. Permanent Finnish resident; travel across EU partner sites as required.
- Built a MATLAB-based automated spectral trending tool used operationally at six monitoring stations for long-term ambient noise characterisation.
- Implemented real-time data quality checks that flag sensor degradation and hardware anomalies before they affect downstream analysis.
- Support integration testing of new sensor hardware prototypes, including calibration of piezoelectric transducers against reference standards.

---

PROJECTS

SoundWatch Environmental Monitoring Dashboard (2021--2022)
Authored the full English-language technical documentation set for the SoundWatch real-time monitoring platform, delivered under the EU QUIETSEA follow-up programme. Presented quarterly status reports in English to Norwegian, Estonian, and Danish project partners. Wrote the user-facing operational manual and the API integration guide used by the Norwegian Shoreline Authority.

---

SKILLS

Signal processing: spectral analysis, wavelet transforms, time-frequency methods, matched filtering
Tools: MATLAB, Simulink, LabVIEW
Domain: underwater acoustics, environmental monitoring, sensor calibration
Languages: Finnish (native), English (working), Hindi (conversational)
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Kaikuvaara's work on spaceborne microwave instruments is what made me stop and read this posting properly. I have followed your contributions to the PolarMet-SG programme from a distance, and the idea of working on hardware that actually ends up in orbit is genuinely compelling.

I have spent the past seven years at Baltic Sensor Networks in Espoo, working on acoustic signal processing for underwater environmental monitoring. The work has been interesting in its own right -- modelling sound propagation in shallow Baltic channels, building spectral analysis tools that run operationally at six monitoring stations, commissioning hydrophone arrays at coastal sites across Finland and the Baltics. But it is not the direction I want for the next stage. I have found myself reading more and more about the remote-sensing missions that Finnish companies contribute to, and Kaikuvaara stands out as a place where the signal processing problems are both technically hard and consequential.

My background is in applied physics from KUT and my day-to-day work over these seven years has been deeply hands-on: I am the person who deals with sensor calibration drift, multipath artefacts in real data, and the gap between simulation and what you actually get from hardware deployed in the field. I believe that engineering instinct transfers, even across domains.

Practically, I would welcome the move to Oulu. My partner is from Oulu originally and we have discussed relocating for some time now. This role would give that plan a real timeline rather than leaving it as something we talk about over dinner. I could be there within six weeks of an offer.

I understand that my experience is in underwater acoustics, not in the RF and radar world. I am not trying to obscure that. What I am saying is that the core work -- extracting reliable signals from noisy physical systems, maintaining calibration integrity, making processing chains that operators can actually trust -- is what I have been doing, and I would bring that with me. I would welcome the chance to talk about whether that kind of transition could work at Kaikuvaara.

Camila Patel

Marie Moreau
marie.moreau@mail.example | +358 00 000 0018 | Tampere

EXPERIENCE

Financial Analyst
Hakala & Rantanen Tilitoimisto, Tampere | June 2024 -- present

- Prepare monthly and quarterly financial reports for a portfolio of 35 SME clients in the Pirkanmaa region.
- Developed internal Excel-based reporting templates that reduced monthly close turnaround from eleven working days to nine.
- Handle VAT filings and annual accounts preparation under Finnish GAAP for clients across manufacturing, retail, and services sectors.
- Coordinate with external auditors during annual reviews; manage client document collection and communication.

EDUCATION

M.Sc. Accounting and Finance
Tammerkoski University | 2024
Thesis: Audit quality determinants in Finnish small and medium enterprises

SKILLS

Financial reporting: Finnish GAAP, IFRS fundamentals, VAT compliance
Tools: SAP Business One, Netvisor, Microsoft Excel (advanced), Power BI
Languages: French (native), Finnish (intermediate -- B1), English (fluent -- all client reporting for international subsidiaries at Hakala & Rantanen conducted in English)
Other: Client relationship management, reconciliation processes, deadline-driven reporting
application.cover_letter_markdown:
In my two years at Hakala & Rantanen, I have been the primary analyst responsible for a portfolio of 35 client accounts, and the work has taught me a few things about delivering consistently under deadline pressure. I am writing because I believe the analytical discipline required in financial reporting translates to engineering environments more directly than people typically assume.

I understand that the Senior Signal Processing Engineer position at Kaikuvaara is a technical role. I have read the posting carefully and I recognise that my background is in finance, not electrical engineering. But I want to make a case for why that might not be the disqualification it first appears.

At Hakala & Rantanen I am responsible for the full reporting cycle for my client portfolio: data collection, reconciliation, analysis, and presentation of results to management. When I started, the monthly close process for some of our more complex manufacturing clients was taking eleven working days. I redesigned the internal reporting templates, introduced structured checklists for the reconciliation stage, and brought that figure down to nine. That is a process-improvement mindset, and the work required understanding the data flows well enough to identify where effort was being wasted.

I also handle international reporting for three clients with Finnish parent companies and subsidiaries abroad. This means working across different accounting standards -- Finnish GAAP and IFRS -- reconciling data from multiple systems, and producing consolidated reports that must withstand audit scrutiny. The stakes are different from signal processing, obviously, but the demand for precision and the consequences of getting it wrong are tangible.

Before joining the firm I completed my Master's in Accounting and Finance at Tammerkoski University, where my thesis examined audit quality in Finnish SMEs. The quantitative methods I applied -- regression analysis, statistical testing on panel data -- were basic by engineering standards, but they gave me a working familiarity with structured data analysis that I have continued to build on since.

What I bring is an ability to take complex, messy information and turn it into reliable, auditable outputs under time pressure. I am a fast learner; I picked up SAP Business One and Netvisor from scratch within my first three months at the firm. Finance has been a solid start to my career, but I want to work on problems where the analytical complexity is the point, not a byproduct of regulatory requirements. I am genuinely interested in moving into a more technically challenging field.

I am aware this is an unconventional application. If there is any scope for a conversation about how my skills might complement the existing team at Kaikuvaara, even in a supporting analytical capacity, I would appreciate the opportunity.

Marie Moreau

application.cover_letter_markdown:
Polaris RF Labs in Helsinki has given me four years of hands-on work across the signal processing chain: embedded C firmware for digital receivers, production Python test infrastructure, phased-array beamforming validation, and signal conditioning for a satellite communication payload. I am writing to Kaikuvaara because the Senior Signal Processing Engineer role looks like it would channel that breadth into systems with real mission weight behind them, and the company's profile -- Finnish-based, genuine space heritage, serious RF instrumentation -- matches what I have been looking for.

My work at Polaris has ranged widely. I started writing channelisation firmware in C for a 16-channel digital receiver on a Xilinx Zynq SoC and building the Python-based factory acceptance test suite that still runs every night against our production receiver boards. My EE degree from Toronto is the foundation I draw on daily for filter design and spectral analysis. Since coming back from a study break in 2023 I have been coordinating a three-person sub-team responsible for calibration and test software, running standups and reviewing merge requests alongside my own technical deliverables. I have also led an RF measurement campaign at the Sodankyla VHF test range and contributed signal conditioning work for a LEO payload prototype under the LINKSAT-2 satellite programme. All of it in an English working environment -- I am the primary author of our customer-facing API documentation and have presented at integration workshops. The range has been good, but what I want now is sustained depth on one programme rather than constant breadth across many.

I should address the career gap. I took 2022--2023 off for further study, primarily machine learning and software engineering courses through open university programmes. It was a planned decision, not a crisis. I returned to Polaris a more effective engineer, particularly in how I think about automated testing and data pipelines, and I make no attempt to hide the gap.

On location: I have been in Helsinki since 2020 with no strong ties to the city beyond the current job. Oulu would be a straightforward relocation for me. I know the area from work trips to the Sodankyla test range, and the concentration of RF and sensor engineering in the region is part of the appeal. My EU Blue Card is renewed through 2026 and I have been continuously employed in Finland since 2020, so work authorisation is not a complication.

What I bring is someone who has built working systems across most of the RF signal processing stack and writes production code in both C and Python. The path has not been linear -- a Canadian EE degree, a study break, a broad role at Polaris -- but the result is an engineer who connects the pieces of a system. I would welcome the chance to discuss the role.

Bartosz Nowak

SUMMARY

EDUCATION

EXPERIENCE

Signal Processing Engineer
Sinikaari Optics, Espoo | February 2024 -- present

- Develop signal conditioning and detection algorithms for the company's automotive LiDAR modules, working across the chain from raw photodetector output through to point-cloud generation.
- All design documentation, code reviews, and customer integration guides written and reviewed in English; primary technical contact for the German Tier-1 customer's engineering team.

PROJECTS

OPAL Phased-Array LiDAR Demonstrator (Sinikaari Optics, 2024--2025)
Designed the beamforming control logic for a 32-element optical phased-array LiDAR transmitter prototype. Implemented the beam-steering algorithm in MATLAB and validated steering accuracy against mechanical scan references at angles up to +/-45 degrees.

NorthStar Point-Cloud Pipeline (Sinikaari Optics, 2025)
Built the production Python pipeline (NumPy, SciPy, pytest) for post-processing raw LiDAR returns into georeferenced point clouds, deployed on the company's edge compute platform with continuous integration. Co-authored a conference paper presented at Pacific Optics Congress 2025 on the coherent detection architecture.

EU LUMINA Consortium Participation
Sinikaari Optics is a partner in the Kestrel Europe LUMINA consortium developing next-generation LiDAR for autonomous maritime navigation. I work alongside teams from Germany, France, and the Netherlands. My employment at Sinikaari is under a standard Finnish employment contract with full EU work rights.

Oulu Suvanto Cold-Weather Test Campaign (August 2025)
Spent two weeks at the Suvanto Oulu facility validating LiDAR module performance in sub-zero conditions. Became familiar with the Oulu engineering community and attended an Oulu Photonics Society event during the trip.

SKILLS

Embedded DSP: C/C++ firmware development for TI TMS320C6748 and FPGA-based LiDAR front-ends; designed and tested real-time signal conditioning kernels for Sinikaari's detector readout boards
Academic foundation: M.Sc. Engineering Physics (Kallavesi, 2023) with coursework in digital signal processing, electromagnetic theory, photonics, and statistical signal analysis
Tools: MATLAB, Simulink, Python (NumPy/SciPy/pytest), Git, Jenkins, Vivado HLS
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Oulu has been on my radar ever since I spent two weeks at the Suvanto facility there last August for cold-weather validation testing on our LiDAR hardware. The engineering community around RF and photonics in the region is more concentrated than I had expected for a city that size, and meeting people from Kaikuvaara's orbit at the Photonics Society event made me start watching your job postings. When the Senior Signal Processing Engineer role appeared, it felt like a direct fit for where I want to take my career.

I am currently at Sinikaari Optics in Espoo, working on signal processing for automotive LiDAR systems. The role covers everything from coherent detection algorithms to production pipeline code, but I am looking for something with greater ambition in terms of platform complexity and mission criticality. Kaikuvaara's work on space-qualified instruments would be exactly that step up.

One area I would highlight is my RF measurement experience. During my thesis work at Kallavesi I characterised the full transmit-receive chain of an FMCW LiDAR prototype using a Keysight UXA signal analyser and a custom optical-to-RF downconversion stage. I did S-parameter measurement of the RF front-end, noise figure characterisation at multiple operating temperatures, and phase noise profiling of the local oscillator across its tuning range. That kind of careful bench measurement is something I find satisfying -- the patience required for a clean calibration and the attention to measurement uncertainty are habits I would bring to instrument-level work at Kaikuvaara.

I also have experience with satellite and airborne platform requirements, which I understand are core to several of Kaikuvaara's current programmes.

On the personal side, I would genuinely welcome a move to Oulu. I already know the city from the Suvanto trip last summer and I liked it -- proper winter, compact and walkable centre, and a technical community that feels connected rather than anonymous. It is somewhere I want to live, not a concession.

I hold an M.Sc. in Engineering Physics from Kallavesi and I have been at Sinikaari since early 2024. The combination of photonics domain knowledge, hands-on signal processing, and production software experience is something I would bring directly to the instrument work at Kaikuvaara. I would welcome the chance to discuss the role.

Anja Kowalski

Sanna Salminen

sanna.salminen@mail.example
Turku

EDUCATION

M.Sc. Electrical Engineering
Roslagen Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm | 2004

EXPERIENCE

Signal Processing Engineer
Fenno Radar Technologies, Turku | 2005 -- present

- Design and implement real-time signal processing algorithms for the company's marine navigation radar product family. Core work involves FMCW waveform processing, target detection, and clutter suppression in varying sea conditions.
- Write production-grade embedded C++ code for the radar processor boards (Analog Devices SHARC DSPs), including real-time FFT processing, CFAR detection, and plot extraction.
- Developed and maintain the Python-based radar simulation and test framework used for regression testing across the full product line. The framework generates synthetic target scenarios, runs them through the processing chain, and validates detection performance against baseline metrics. Runs nightly in CI.

PROJECTS

4-Element UHF Beamforming Demonstrator (Personal project, 2023--2024)
Built a small phased-array receive demonstrator using four discone antennas, an RTL-SDR array, and a custom GNURadio flowgraph for real-time beamforming at 435 MHz. The system can steer a null roughly +/-30 degrees from boresight. Used it to learn the basics of array calibration and spatial filtering. It is a hobby setup -- breadboard construction, consumer SDR dongles, many evenings of work -- but it gave me first-hand experience with mutual coupling effects and calibration stability that I would not have picked up from reading alone.

Marine Radar Antenna Pattern Measurement (Fenno Radar Technologies, 2019)
Performed RF pattern measurements on the company's X-band slotted-waveguide antenna using a Rohde & Schwarz ZVA67 network analyser and a compact antenna test range at the Turku facility. Produced the qualified antenna patterns and co-polar/cross-polar isolation data used for the CE compliance filing.

SKILLS

Technical: FMCW radar signal processing, target detection (CFAR), clutter filtering, FFT-based spectral analysis
Programming: SHARC assembly, C++, Python, MATLAB
Publications: S. Salminen et al., "Adaptive clutter map for X-band marine radar," SESE Radar Conference 2018 (conference paper)
Nationality: Finnish citizen, EU work authorisation
application.cover_letter_markdown:
After twenty years building radar signal processing systems at Fenno Radar Technologies in Turku, I am looking at what comes next. I have spent my career on one product family at one employer, which has given me depth but has also meant I have not had the breadth of exposure I might have liked. The Senior Signal Processing Engineer role at Kaikuvaara caught my attention because it sits at the junction of skills I have developed over two decades and systems I have always wanted to work on.

My day-to-day at Fenno Radar is hands-on signal processing for marine navigation radar. FMCW waveform design, embedded DSP on Analog Devices SHARC processors in C++, CFAR detection, and clutter suppression algorithms that have to work in sea conditions no model fully predicts. I also built and maintain the production Python test framework the engineering team uses to validate detection performance across the product line. The work is real, and I am proud of what the products do. But marine radar is a mature category now, and the problems I face today are incremental refinements of problems I solved a decade ago.

What draws me to Kaikuvaara is the RF and photonics community in Oulu. I have followed the cluster of companies and research groups in the region for several years, and the concentration of radar and RF work there stands out in the Nordics. Kaikuvaara in particular does the kind of instrument-level engineering where signal processing decisions are inseparable from hardware realities and mission requirements. That kind of problem is what I find most rewarding.

My education at RRIT prepared me well for this work. I completed my M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering in Stockholm in 2004, specialising in signals and systems. The coursework in spectral analysis, detection theory, and waveform design has been the most durable asset across twenty years of practical radar engineering, more useful in hindsight than any specific tool or language. The thesis examined spectral methods for wideband communications, but the mathematical core transferred directly to the radar processing I went on to do at Fenno.

I should mention a side project that may be relevant. Over the past two years I have been building a 4-element phased-array receive demonstrator at home: four discone antennas, RTL-SDR receivers, and a GNURadio flowgraph for real-time beamsteering at 435 MHz. It is firmly a hobby setup -- breadboard construction, consumer SDR dongles, many evenings of debugging mutual coupling artefacts. The system can steer a null about 30 degrees off boresight and I have used it for amateur radio direction finding, but the real value has been the intuition it built for how array performance degrades in practice versus simulation. I do not want to overstate what it is, but the problems it surfaced were more instructive than I expected.

I would welcome the chance to discuss how my background fits the role.

Sanna Salminen

- All technical documentation and customer-facing deliverables produced in English; act as primary technical contact for the company's UK-based maritime data customers.

PROJECTS

SEASTAR Coastal Phased-Array Receiver (Baltic Sensor Networks, 2018--2020)
Implemented a digital beamforming algorithm for a 16-element L-band phased-array receiver used in a coastal maritime surveillance prototype. Wrote the spatial filtering and beam-scheduling code in C for a TI C6678 multi-core DSP, achieving real-time operation at 10 MHz sampling per channel.

MarineSight Automated Detection Pipeline (Baltic Sensor Networks, 2021--2023)
Built the production Python pipeline (SciPy, NumPy, Celery, PostgreSQL) for automated ship detection from SAR imagery. The system processes incoming satellite passes, performs CFAR detection, and generates alert feeds for port authority customers. Deployed on cloud infrastructure, handling approximately 200 satellite passes per day.

Oulujoki University CubeSat Ground Station RF Characterisation (2009--2010)
Performed RF characterisation of the university's CubeSat ground station UHF receive chain as part of my master's thesis work. Used an Agilent E5071C network analyser for S-parameter measurement of the LNA cascade and filter stages. Measured antenna radiation patterns on the university's rooftop range using a calibrated signal source and rotator-mounted reference dipole. Documented noise temperature contributions across the receive chain. This work was done entirely within the university radio laboratory with no industrial partner or external funding.

M.Sc. Thesis: UHF Ground Station Link Budget Analysis (Oulujoki University, 2010)
Validated the downlink link budget for the university's 1U CubeSat mission, applying signal processing and RF chain modelling from the Electrical Engineering programme to a practical system design problem.

Baltic Sensor Networks Oulu Facility (2015--2017)
Participated in establishing the company's Oulu satellite data processing centre, setting up the operational infrastructure for near-real-time SAR data reception and processing. Have been based at the Oulu site since it opened.

application.cover_letter_markdown:
Satellite radar data arrives from orbit as a stream of raw I/Q samples, and for the past fifteen years at Baltic Sensor Networks it has been my job to turn that stream into maritime surveillance products that port authorities and coastguards actually use. I know the output of spaceborne SAR instruments intimately, but I have never worked on the instruments themselves. That is what I want to change, and Kaikuvaara is the obvious place in Oulu to do it.

At Baltic Sensor Networks I have worked across the processing chain: radiometric calibration and geocoding of SAR imagery, CFAR-based ship detection for automated alerting, beamforming for a coastal phased-array receiver prototype, and the production Python pipeline that processes our daily satellite data throughput. The breadth has been valuable. But what I want now is to move upstream, closer to the sensor itself, to the place where the algorithm meets the antenna and the physics of the measurement matter most.

The mission-critical nature of Kaikuvaara's instruments is what makes the role particularly compelling to me. When hardware must survive launch and operate autonomously for years in orbit, the signal processing design choices carry a weight that ground-based processing simply does not demand. I find that kind of constraint motivating rather than daunting -- it forces clarity about what matters.

My RF measurement foundations come from my master's at the Oulujoki University, where I spent a year on the CubeSat ground station project. I did S-parameter characterisation of the UHF receive chain with an Agilent network analyser and measured antenna radiation patterns on the rooftop range. It was university-scale work, no industrial partner, but it was thorough and careful, and it gave me hands-on measurement experience I have always wanted to build on in a professional setting.

I have been in Oulu since 2006 and I consider it home. I know the RF and sensing engineering community here, and Kaikuvaara's presence is one of the things that gives it critical mass. Contributing to that from inside the company, rather than from the data-processing end of the chain, would be a meaningful change for me. I would welcome the chance to discuss how my experience fits the role.

Fatima Reddy

application.cover_letter_markdown:
The engineering scene in Oulu was one of the reasons I moved here from Delft in 2024. I had been following the growth of the RF and photonics cluster in the region and it felt like one of the few places in Northern Europe where that kind of work was actively expanding rather than just maintaining what already existed. I knew the job opportunities in my own field of industrial design would be fewer up here than in the Randstad, but I was willing to make that trade for the chance to be closer to a different kind of engineering.

I realise my background is not the conventional path to a signal processing role. My degree from TU Maasdelta is in Industrial Design Engineering and the gap between that and what Kaikuvaara does is obvious. But I have spent the past year and a half at Baltic Sensor Networks in Oulu doing operational work with sensor systems -- monitoring underwater acoustic arrays, maintaining data ingestion pipelines, writing documentation for international partners -- and the experience has confirmed that this is the field I want to build a career in.

What appeals to me about Kaikuvaara is the precision of the engineering. From what I have read about your instruments, the care required to account for environmental effects, component drift, and all the real-world factors that separate a working measurement system from a simulation is the kind of problem-solving I find genuinely compelling. I know I am not the person solving those problems today. But I want to be working alongside the people who are, and learning from them.

I should address the gap on my CV directly. I was out from January 2025 through April 2026 recovering from a serious illness. I have been back at work since May and I am fully fit. It is not something I try to conceal.

My strongest practical asset is the ability to learn new technical domains quickly. When I arrived at Baltic Sensor Networks I had no background in sensor systems at all, and within a few months I was maintaining the data quality infrastructure for the network. I built operational monitoring dashboards in Python that the team relies on daily. The systematic design training from TU Maasdelta turned out to be more transferable to technical operational work than either I or my employer had expected.

I am based in Oulu and intend to stay. If there is room for someone willing to build depth on the job, I would welcome the conversation.

Omar Kim

application.cover_letter_markdown:
This application probably looks unusual, so I will be upfront about it. I am a frontend developer with twenty-two years of web development experience, not a signal processing engineer. But I have been thinking about changing direction for some time, and the engineering community in Oulu keeps coming up as somewhere genuinely interesting things are happening.

I have worked at Kirkaspiste Studios in Helsinki since 2004, joining straight after my degree in Visual Communication Design at Bukak National University. The studio was tiny then, three people, and I have grown with it. Over the years I have gone from building static HTML sites through the jQuery and Backbone.js era into the modern world of React, TypeScript, and component-driven architecture. The constants across two decades have been an emphasis on clean, maintainable code and a strong instinct for visual and interaction design.

My clients have included Finnish retail chains, public-sector web portals, and several SaaS products. All of the work has been conducted in English, which is the primary working language at the studio -- used for every client communication, code review, and piece of technical documentation we produce. After twenty-two years I know how to take ambiguous requirements and deliver reliable software on deadline, and I believe that discipline transfers.

Beyond frontend code, I have set up CI/CD pipelines for our client projects, built automated end-to-end testing suites, handled deployment infrastructure, and done the performance profiling work that keeps applications responsive under production load. I am comfortable across the full delivery chain, not only the visual layer, and I think that breadth matters more than the specific technology when moving into a new domain.

Why consider leaving a field where I am well established? Honestly, web development has started to feel like solving variations of the same problem with increasingly elaborate tooling. I want to work on something where the underlying physics matters, where software has to interact with real hardware and the physical world rather than a browser engine. I do not underestimate what that shift requires. But I have navigated steep transitions before: I took two years of parental leave in 2011--2013 and came back to find the entire frontend ecosystem had changed beneath me. I was productive again within months.

The RF and photonics community in Oulu has caught my attention because of the concentration of serious engineering work in a relatively compact city. The engineering density is unusual for a Nordic city of that size, and from what I can gather, Kaikuvaara is at the centre of it. I do not know whether there is a realistic path from web frontend into the work you do. But if there is a software-adjacent need -- tooling, visualisation, test infrastructure -- where engineering quality matters as much as specific domain pedigree, I would be very interested to talk.

Leila Okafor
